taskVersion.name: pilot-ves-label-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Egwi, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 295.88 | 0.54518 | 0.54518
2 | 798.6 | 3.5924 | 4.1376
3 | 864.62 | 2.1559 | 6.2935
4 | 1810.2 | 37.957 | 37.25
5 | 5634.2 | - | -

What is the curve type of this station? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve type, we look at the resistivity of the five layers:
- Layer 1: 295.88 ohm-m
- Layer 2: 798.6 ohm-m
- Layer 3: 864.62 ohm-m
- Layer 4: 1810.2 ohm-m
- Layer 5: 5634.2 ohm-m

Next, we examine each group of three consecutive layers:
1.  **Layers 1-2-3**: 295.88 < 798.6 < 864.62. This follows the $r_1 < r_2 < r_3$ pattern, so the letter is **A**.
2.  **Layers 2-3-4**: 798.6 < 864.62 < 1810.2. This follows the $r_1 < r_2 < r_3$ pattern, so the letter is **A**.
3.  **Layers 3-4-5**: 864.62 < 1810.2 < 5634.2. This follows the $r_1 < r_2 < r_3$ pattern, so the letter is **A**.

The full sequence of letters is AAA. Since all the letters are the same, the curve type can be written as the single letter A.

{"curve_type": "A"}
